name: OutFit
description: Restyle any website by describing the change in plain language.
_comment_all_urls: <all_urls> is here for dark mode and nothing else. The engine (vendor/darkreader.js) is 354KB and most pages never ask for it, so it is injected on demand rather than listed in content_scripts - and injecting into a tab on page load is not a user gesture, so activeTab cannot cover it. This adds no warning at install: content_scripts already matches <all_urls>, which is the same sentence Chrome shows.
_comment_options_ui: The one setting that is about OutFit rather than about the page in front of you - whether usage is shared - lives here rather than in the settings card the panel opens. open_in_tab is false on purpose: Chrome then shows options.html as a sheet inside chrome://extensions, which is the only place it appears at all, and closing it returns you to the extensions list instead of leaving a stray tab open.

open-prompt._comment_key: Alt+K, and measured rather than picked. Chrome flatly refuses Command+Period, +D, +Y and +G - it keeps those - and it hands over Command+B, +U and +Comma, which is worse, since taking those steals the bookmarks bar, view-source and preferences. Command+Space registers and then never fires, because Spotlight is in front of the browser. That leaves Command+K, which Chrome does not want but every command palette on the web does - Slack, Linear, Notion, GitHub, Figma - and an extension shortcut beats the page, so OutFit would silently break search on exactly the sites a heavy user has open. Alt+K is the one two-key combination nobody is holding: Chrome has no use for it, and web apps avoid Option+letter because on a Mac it types a character rather than firing a handler.
open-prompt.description: Open the OutFit prompt on this page

web_accessible_resources._comment: popup.html and nothing else. The panel frames it inside the page, which is what this list is for. Everything popup.html then loads - popup.css, popup.js, providers.js, builtin.js, the icons - is fetched by an extension-origin document and needs no entry here; report-file.js has always been loaded that way and has never been listed. Listing them anyway made them readable by any website, and builtin.js is the file a key goes in when the proxy is not used.
